Gnosis Interpretation
MOVE tracks Treasury volatility and term-premium stress: below 80 is calm, 80-120 is moderate uncertainty, and 150+ is high stress; 108.13 is moderate. SOFR is secured overnight funding (3.90% effective Sep 30), not a stand-alone stress verdict. NFCI measures broad financial conditions; its -0.55 reading indicates looser conditions. The 10Y yield at 5.24% is down 5 bp on the latest Treasury session.

Fed & Policy Watch
  • Today's 8:30 AM ET Employment Situation (September) is the dominant labor-market catalyst. FOMC minutes from Sep 15-16 follow Oct 7 at 2:00 PM ET; minutes are not a rate decision.
  • Oct 6: New York Fed President Williams moderates a public event at 9:05 AM; no prepared text expected. EIA releases its October Short-Term Energy Outlook and Winter Fuels Outlook between 12:00 and 12:15 PM.
  • New York Fed Treasury operations for Sep 15-Oct 14 plan about $15.6B in reinvestment purchases and no reserve-management purchases; routine liquidity backdrop, not a one-time injection.
  • Policy headline watch: the White House U.S.-China Board of Trade (Sep 27) identifies product lists for possible reciprocal reduced-tariff treatment, subject to domestic law and process. No implementation date is specified; treat any change as headline risk, not a timed catalyst.
  • Cboe lists expanded weekly options expirations on Oct 2 and Oct 9; NYSE shows no cash-session holiday or shortened session through Oct 9.
Omissions and Watch
  • BLS direct schedule request returned HTTP 403. The official BLS October list and Employment Situation release-specific calendar were readable via official web fallback: September Employment Situation is today, Oct 2 at 8:30 AM ET. CPI is Oct 14 and PPI Oct 15, both outside this Oct 2-9 window.
  • NY Fed calendar dates Initial Claims Oct 8 at 8:30 AM ET; its linked DOL data endpoint timed out in the prior date-specific check, so the release date/time is verified but report-week detail is unavailable.
  • EIA confirms Natural Gas Storage next release Oct 8 at 10:30 AM ET and Heating Oil & Propane next release Oct 7 at 1:00 PM ET. EIA WPSR did not expose a date-specific Oct 7 release in its current page, so no petroleum-inventory row is inferred from weekly cadence.
  • TreasuryDirect upcoming-auction data confirms Oct 5-8 bill, note, and bond auction dates and bid cutoffs; note/bond cutoffs are 12:00 PM noncompetitive and 1:00 PM competitive. No inferred issuance rows are used.
  • BEA lists Services Supplied Through Affiliates (2024) on Oct 6 at 10:00 AM; omitted as an annual structural dataset with limited immediate ES/rates sensitivity. NY Fed also lists Weekly Economic Index Oct 8, Economic Heterogeneity Indicators and Staff Nowcast Oct 2, and Staff Nowcast Oct 9; omitted as routine weekly/model indicators. Routine H.15 and commercial-paper tables are likewise omitted.
  • NAR lists no housing release through Oct 9 (next existing-home sales is Oct 13). NYSE calendar shows no U.S. cash-market holiday or shortened session through Oct 9; Columbus Day closure is Oct 12, outside this window. Sep 30 quarter-end has passed.
  • Market snapshot uses one delayed Yahoo Finance source; quotes are labeled by observation/session. No unavailable quote was substituted or inferred.
Trading Strategy Note | ES Futures
BASE CASE
Keep risk sized for today's 8:30 AM Employment Situation; the report can reprice both growth and policy expectations. The 10Y yield is down 5 bp and MOVE remains moderate; require ES price confirmation before treating the overnight move as durable. Scenario framework, not a directional forecast.
INVALIDATION
Reassess a range or continuation thesis if ES breaks and holds outside the overnight range with confirming Treasury-yield/volatility repricing, or if payrolls materially shifts the expected policy path. Not a trade signal.
